newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower in very light trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower in very light trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities declined modestly in thin trading on a very quiet Monday, traders said.
Thirty-year pass-throughs generally were off 1/32 to 2/32 by late on Monday afternoon.
A dearth of economic events made for a very quiet market, according to traders. "We've been near dead," one trader said. "Rigor mortis has set in."
Activity may remain sparse for the next several days, with no key data set for release, market participants said. "It's going to be an extremely quiet week," said one trader.
Spreads over Treasuries largely held intact on Monday.

Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent coupons had slipped 1/32 to 99-22/32 and were yielding 110 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was off 1/32 as well, at 99-20/32 and 99-25/42, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 3/32 at 99-28/32, yielding 6.52 percent.
Reports on September import and export prices, and possibly the September Treasury budget, are scheduled for release on Tuesday.
